system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:28 UTC, FILE-NWD-01 opened an HTTP-classified connection to the explicit proxy PROXY-NWD-01 and sent 640,000,221 bytes; the connection lasted about 12 seconds and completed normally.

The transfer volume is compatible with the supplied description of approved offsite backups, but this record identifies only the proxy as the immediate destination—not the external service, URL, or uploading process.

A Kerberos service-ticket event recorded svc-archive requesting a ticket for FILE-NWD-01 from source IP 139.162.174.124, an address outside the supplied internal network context. This is suspicious, but the record does not establish why the request occurred or whether it is connected to the transfer.

Nora Blake launched Remote Desktop from WS-NBLAKE-01 to FILE-NWD-01 at 13:34:28 UTC; the recorded RDP connection lasted about 785 seconds and overlapped the large proxy flow. The evidence does not show that the RDP session caused or initiated the transfer.

The supplied operational practice says remote administration is performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01, whereas the recorded RDP connection originated from WS-NBLAKE-01. This discrepancy warrants investigation, but the records alone do not establish malicious intent or the actions taken in the session.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied coverage status reports that FILE-NWD-01 winsec and sysmon logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC; this includes the transfer and the scheduled svc-render password-rotation period.
The supplied coverage status reports that proxy logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, preventing confirmation of the HTTP destination, URL, and proxy transaction details.
Zeek connection telemetry records the large flow to the proxy, but the available record does not identify the originating process or final external destination.
